title: Day one: the bath moves to the side garden
body: The bird bath started out the front, tucked into a shrub, and the birds loved it. The front faces a road and a school, though, so it moved to the side garden: enclosed, quieter, and right under a big tree the birds already use.

It keeps its solar fountain, because moving water brings birds in and sounds lovely on camera. A potted tree and a bushy shrub go either side for cover, with a branch to perch on and a flat stone so the smallest birds can stand in shallow water.

title: The camera goes up, and the stream goes live
body: A weatherproof camera now sits on a shelf on the house wall, framed on the bath and nothing else: no street, no school, no neighbours. It streams to YouTube around the clock, with the real sound of the garden.

The setup got a few upgrades along the way: the bath now stands in a pot of rocks so it can't tip, an old pallet makes a backdrop with two hanging water dishes, and a trellis and a timber post give birds somewhere to perch before they drink.

title: Next: every visit, logged automatically
body: The camera will save a short clip whenever something lands. Each clip gets identified (bird, how many, what it did) and added to the visitors log.

title: Next: native plants for cover
body: A grevillea for the honeyeaters and a westringia for the little birds to hide in.

title: Later: a fish pond
body: More water, more habitat, and hopefully frogs. It gets its own write-up when it happens.
